Sports.title: Jordan Nobbs ready to complete wishlist with Newcastle WSL dream
Sports.content:
Jordan Nobbs says winning promotion to the Women’s Super League with Newcastle would fulfil her ambition for a north‑east club to be in the top tier.

Nobbs, who has 71 England caps, was born in Stockton‑on‑Tees and believes women’s football in the region would benefit immensely from top‑flight representation. Newcastle finished sixth in WSL2 last season, 11 points behind the title winners, Birmingham, and nine points off the playoffs, but this summer they have made their hopes clear with high-calibre signings from the top division, including the striker Martha Thomas from Tottenham and the Liverpool duo Leanne Kiernan and Gemma Evans.

Nobbs is clear about the target for the new campaign. “It is promotion. I know we said it last season [too],” she said. “I’ve always said things don’t happen overnight, [but] that is our goal. You have to say it out loud.

“Looking back on last season, we had some really good performances but nine draws, that’s too many points [dropped]. It’s just about focusing on finding a way to win. We’ve just got to build on the good stuff from last season, I don’t think we’re far off it.

“[Winning promotion with Newcastle], I’ve always said it would be job done. I think to get a northern team promoted … as I heard from Newcastle I was like, that is exactly what I want to do. In the WSL, I’d ticked as much as I possibly could, so to get a north‑east team, which we all had to leave back in the day, promoted would be an achievement I would love.”

Nobbs began her career with Sunderland and broke into their team in the old top flight, but moved to Arsenal when the WSL was launched in 2011 and Sunderland’s application to join the breakaway division was rejected. That led to a successful team also including Nobbs’s future England teammates Lucy Bronze and Lucy Staniforth breaking up.

Sunderland did compete in the top tier between 2015 and 2018, but north-east representation in the WSL has been sparse, so Nobbs is pleased to see investment in recent years at Newcastle as well as their WSL2 rivals, who were taken over in June by Bay Collective.

“It’s been a long time coming, but it was something us northerners have always wanted,” Nobbs said. “We don’t want the north-east to fizzle out. We want to show the players that have come from there and developed there.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It’s definitely grown in the right direction now, which is what we wanted. But the big stepping stone would be getting into the WSL. That would be where we really put the north-east back on the map and I’d love to be a part of that.”

The 33-year-old has enjoyed her role in Tanya Oxtoby’s setup at Newcastle after joining them last July. “With Villa I played a lot of a deeper role and [now] I really love being back in my high position, scoring goals, assisting and [I’m] in my happy place. I feel like I found that little spark again [last season] that was nice.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille who value Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of signing Rodri from City, but they will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint‑Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30‑year‑old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester player Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of securing a deal for the 18-year-old midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post‑World Cup break. The 28-year-old has spent the past season and a half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa respectively, in the aftermath of a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former United head coach Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the United manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Man United's lack of transfer business risks undermining all their good work under Ineos. It's time to back up talk of grand plans with action - or fans' patience will run out, writes NATHAN SALT
Sports.content:
Heading into the summer transfer window, the expectation outside of Manchester United was that this was a club ready to splash the cash. A third-place finish - and crucially a return to Champions League football - was to be supplemented by a record-breaking access fee for Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary, a record training kit sponsorship with Betway, upticks in sponsorship deals with existing partners and huge salaries for the likes of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho now officially off the books. All signs pointed to a £200million midfield rebuild, with players of the quality of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Mateus Fernandes and Aurelien Tchouameni on the shortlist, to help transform United back into one of England and Europe’s elite. After the club's newlook recruitment team hit the mark with four summer signings a year ago, transforming the club’s fortunes in attack and in goal, excitement was through the roof. But now, as United’s players and staff enjoy a five-day training and team-bonding retreat in Ireland, fingers are again being pointed at the powers-that-be by supporters. Just how serious are you about competing with the very best? Man United's decision-makers (from left to right) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are starting to come under pressure from fans over a lack of transfer activity Actions speak louder than words There are a handful of things that Ineos and the decision-makers at Manchester United love. They love to tell supporters about the ‘clear plan’ to take them back to contending for Premier League titles. They love self-imposed frugality and how that shift in approach no longer leaves United open to being a pawn in the game of chess that is the transfer window. And they love project players in the mould of Chido Obi, Ayden Heaven, Sekou Kone, Enzo Kana-Biyik, Diego Leon, Cristian Orozco and Tynan Thompson. ‘We have a clear plan,’ director of football Jason Wilcox said back in October. ‘I am sure there are going to be bumps in the road but we have just got to make sure we stay calm irrespective of the noise outside.’ Only this summer, that same phrase was repeated by chief executive Omar Berrada through the club’s internal podcast arm Inside Carrington. ‘We have a clear plan,’ Berrada said. ‘[Director of football] Jason Wilcox and his team are well set up to execute that plan. ‘What we saw last season is a good way forward for us. We want a mix of experience and youth. A mix of players who have demonstrated they can perform in the Premier League and players that are doing very well outside the Premier League. ‘Whatever decisions we take will not just be for the short term but the long term.’ The issue Manchester United are facing is that talking about a plan doesn't represent fun for supporters.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Restraint isn’t fun. Projects tend to be a slow process that take years to pay off, with the likes of Leon, Orozco and Kana-Biyik some way off first team football. Fans of any club crave the dopamine rush a new transfer provides. The transfer window has become an addictive loop of rumour and reward, and the absence of business quickly causes inquests online. And there is some legitimacy to the frustrations of many United fans. They didn’t get Anderson, their undisputed No 1 target. He ended up at Manchester City in a £116million record-breaking deal for an English midfielder. An obvious ‘bump in the road’, as Wilcox put it. They didn’t get Mateus Fernandes, a player that felt much more attainable internally before the finances involved exploded and Ineos’ frugality kicked in. He ended up at Tottenham Hotspur for £85million. United were frustrated that the player didn’t push more to end up at Old Trafford. Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali have both long been admired but figures close to both parties have explained to Daily Mail Sport how any hope United would get close to the financials to land one of Newcastle's star men was quickly extinguished under their new, more austere regime. They ended up at Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur for a combined £175million. ‘We have to be really disciplined. We have a plan, we know what we can invest and we need to stick to it,’ Berrada added back in June. ‘In some cases, we may decide to make an investment knowing it is the right thing, not for the next two or three years but the next ten. ‘We need to stay very focused on what we are trying to achieve. It's very important you don't let the market or the agents dictate what we should be doing.’ The final line is the kicker. In a market where the base price for a good-to-great Premier League midfielder is around £75-80million, United are determined not to fall into the traps of the previous regime, where big-money signings would lead to years of expensive repayments, all for little-to-no on-pitch success. United pivoted to Aston Villa's Youri Tielemans, triggering his release clause. It was a smart signing As was the addition of Andrey Santos from Chelsea. But United need more numbers in midfield So, United pivoted. First to Andrey Santos, a player United first brought up to Chelsea when the terms of Alejandro Garnacho’s move were discussed a year ago, before finally getting him for £50million earlier this summer. Then it was Youri Tielemans, triggering his £35million release clause. Having landed the Premier League's official ‘Signing of the Season’ in Senne Lammens last term, internally there is a belief that his fellow Belgian Tielemans can make it two-for-two in 2026-27. Both are smart signings with huge upside. Adding to Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko and Lammens, Ineos can point to a track record of their way being a successful one. Internally, too, there has been a real eagerness to no longer be seen as a club that can be ripped off, a club that agents can manipulate or bully. This was one of the main reasons they didn’t cave on their valuation of Jorge Mendes client Fernandes when Tottenham upped the ante. The desire to limit leaks is stronger than ever, too. Wilcox and Berrada have placed immense emphasis on acting in the shadows and out of the court of public opinion. The Tielemans signing appeared to outsiders to come from nowhere, much to the delight of bosses. They have been decisive in moving on from Rasmus Hojlund, in getting all the wages covered in the loans for Andre Onana (Trabzonspor) and Altay Bayindir (Celta Vigo), and insiders believe United are close to escaping the dreaded cycle of being seen as a poor recruiter, blinded by star power. But with three weeks left to go in this transfer window, Ineos and United’s decision makers are at a crossroads. It’s an expensive market and Michael Carrick needs more. With Champions League football on the horizon, and the first seven games coming in a 29-day stretch, Carrick needs help. United proved against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg that they are ready to be aggressive on the pitch, with their exciting style of play. The question now is, can Ineos be aggressive off it? With his team set to play seven games in the first 29 days of the new season, Michael Carrick needs more quality players to call upon So, where do they need to strengthen? Signing a left back is absolutely essential. Two enquiries to Newcastle United for Lewis Hall – both strongly rebuffed – show that United know that, too. For as much credit as Luke Shaw deserves for starting every single Premier League game last season, asking him to replicate it amid the added strain of European football feels like wishful thinking. The options in front of United are to make a big play for Hall, a player that could be United’s and England’s left back for the next decade. Newcastle will want record money for a full back. That won’t change. Or there is the youth route, promoting Harry Amass, who has looked bright during pre-season. Yet he has been told his best chance for regular game-time is elsewhere. United are understood to be open to both loan and permanent deals. And then there is the cheap option of keeping faith with Shaw and leaning on Noussair Mazraoui, who plays left back for Morocco, in case of injury. Luke Shaw deserves credit for starting every Premier League game last season. But to expect him to do the same in 2026-27 feels like wishful thinking Lewis Hall would be an ambitious and exciting signing at left back. But United's efforts so far haven't extended beyond an enquiry Only one of those three options would signal that United are heading towards the very top, and it’s not options two or three. Patrick Dorgu, despite being listed as a defender in every squad list, is only seen as an option further forward on the wing. Then there is the conundrum of the midfield, and whether United do or don’t need a third recruit in that area (they do). Mason Mount, who has been a huge success across pre-season, came off in Gothenburg after 20 minutes and that highlighted the fragility of United’s side just a fortnight out from the season. Mount is popular with every manager he plays under but his reliability is an issue. He has started just 25 league games since joining United for £55million three years ago. Tielemans, as exciting a signing as he is, missed over 20 games with injury last season. Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee and the plan was to move him on. Casemiro has gone. Santos is a smart addition and Kobbie Mainoo will rightly be an important figure. But United need another body. Shifting too much onus, too soon onto the likes of Tyler Fletcher, who is expected to be the young midfielder United place the most effort into developing for the first team this season, is unfair. ‘For us to get in the top four and consistently challenge for Champions League places, win the Champions League, win the Premier League, we have got to invest in the squad,’ Wilcox said back in that October sit-down. ‘We have got to buy the right players.’ And so far they’ve done that. Of the 13 first-team signings to this point under Ineos, only Ugarte has proven a major disappointment. In bringing in (from left) Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha last summer, Ineos worked wonders in the transfer market. But they need to be more active this time around But if Project 150 – the stated aim of winning the Premier League title by 2028 in United’s 150th anniversary year – is legitimate and not just a piece of catchy PR, United face a defining three weeks to set the tone for where they are going. Ineos deserve trust and patience to navigate ‘bumps in the road’ after their success in moving on the deadwood, bringing down the wage bill, transforming the team’s fortunes with hits in the transfer market, and committing to plans for a new stadium. But patience doesn’t last for ever and if, in three weeks' time, United are still light in midfield, relying on Shaw as a sole left back option, and there is no back-up to Sesko, don’t be surprised if many fans' patience has run out.

Sports.title: James McClean's dream return to hometown club turns into a nightmare: Derry City attempt to rip up poppy-protest footballer's contract - with defiant star, 37, set for training ground showdown
Sports.content:
James McClean's homecoming story looks to have taken a sour turn after his club informed the 37-year-old that they intended to rip up his contract due to a perceived lack of 'physical capacity' required to fulfil its terms.

McClean, who has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations, signed for his hometown club Derry City at the start of the 2026 season.

But, according to the Irish Independent, the club have told McClean they are ending his contract despite it still having two years left to run, claiming he is unable to fulfil its terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

The report states that McClean disputes that assessment and is keen to continue playing, with the former Wrexham full back still set to report for training this week.

McClean, who has started just 12 of sixth-placed Derry City's 27 league games this season, is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally and that an independent physician is required to determine his fitness, the report states.

It has been a turbulent few weeks for McClean, who has regularly taken to social media to criticise his side. He also posted a picture showing he was watching former side Wrexham play a Carabao Cup match at the same time Derry City were playing a home league game.

McClean, who has started just 12 of sixth-placed Derry City's 27 league games this season, is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

In June, the 37-year-old hinted at his unhappiness following his return home after a 15-year spell in English football.

'Family (are) enjoying being home – probably not so much myself, if I’m being honest,' McClean said during a punditry appearance on RTE.

'You know, you have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and you quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

'There’s a lot of factors that’s contributed to that, but we’ll leave them for another day.'

McClean has previously spoken out about his reasons for not wearing the poppy, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012. He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean said in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour world war 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both world wars.

McClean, who has won more than 100 caps for Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he had received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won more than 100 caps for Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy," and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

Sports.title: There's a new Team GB sprint Queen! Amy Hunt dethrones Dina Asher-Smith and storms to 100m European gold - and there could be more to come
Sports.content:
Sprint sensation Amy Hunt continued her sizzling summer by storming to a landmark European gold in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old clocked 11.00s to land her first major individual triumph and dethrone reigning champion Dina Asher-Smith, who finished fifth.

'I was getting fed up of silver,' said Hunt, who finished second in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow. 'It is so special to do this at home.

'I had such a big premonition, and I just love my job. This is what makes it the best.

'I just had such a magical feeling. I've won English Schools here, I've raced here as a kind of 13, 14-year-old, so, this is really my track. I'm a girl, I'm from Newark, so I just had a feeling that this was going to be my night.

'My first gold. I think it was definitely time for an upgrade. I think this was definitely a coming of age for me here tonight, and I'm now kind of fully established.

'I'm a 100m medallist, I've got two 100m medals in the last two weeks, and one more sub-11 to boot. I'm very, very happy.'

Hunt narrowly held off Poland's Eva Swoboda, who finished two-hundredths of a second behind, with Belgium's Delphine Nkansa earning bronze.

Amy Hunt is the new European champion after taking gold in the 100m sprint

Grantham rocket Amy Hunt will be competing across four fronts in Birmingham this week

It is the start of what she hopes will be a historic week as she targets gold on four fronts, with the 200m - in which she won World Championship silver last year - and a pair of relays to come.

'I want to be the best. I don't shy away from that. I train incredibly hard, and I back myself so incredibly hard. I'm not saying that I'm the best right now, but that's something I aspire to be.'

Hunt set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 10.99s to ease into the showpiece.

Reigning champion Asher-Smith also made it through but could only play a bit part in the final on this occasion in the latest sign of a shift in the balance of power within British sprinting.

'The stage of a final doesn’t intimidate me and I just knew I had to stay calm and not overthink myself into the goal,' Hunt said.

'That was why the Commonwealths really came in handy for me. That’s why I really wanted to do it, to have that experience of being in front of a home crowd, having that medal expectation, because I've never had that before.'

Hunt credited the unlikely trio of Megan Thee Stallion, High School Musical and Mamma Mia as key to keeping her calm in the build-up, along with keeping her brain active on Wordle.

As in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow, her start left her with catching up to do but she never had cause to press the panic button.

'One of my biggest skills in terms of championships is I know I'm so strong in the end and I always have that kind of extra magic in the last 40,' she said.

'It can definitely rescue me in situations that I've got myself into but I kind of know the distance I can be away from the girls in order to be able to come back.

'I did leave it a little bit last minute this time but in championships, it's all about crossing the line first.

'When I look back at this race in 10 years, I'm not going to think about how far back I was after 30 metres.'

Hunt returns to action on Wednesday in her ‘favourite event’, the 200m. Her plans before that are refreshingly simple.

'Try to get as much sleep as possible and a big fat lie-in.' After this, she has earned it.

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle
Sports.content:
Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan with an option to buy.

The 27-year-old defender flew to Merseyside on Sunday afternoon and has since completed his medical.

The Reds have the option to purchase the Uruguay international at the end of the campaign for £47million.

'I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy,' Araujo said.

'I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my teammates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

'I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

'As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time.'

Liverpool have confirmed the loan signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo

The Uruguayan defender has joined the Anfield club on a season long loan

Araujo added that he will take inspiration from 'role model' Virgil van Dijk when he lines up alongside the Liverpool captain.

'We all know what a great player Virgil is. He's a real reference point for the team and he's a kind of role model and reference for me personally as well,' he told the club's website.

'I am excited to have that opportunity and enjoy learning from him, playing alongside him. With hard work, I think we can achieve good things together as a partnership and as a defence.'

Defence was an area which needed strengthening following the departure of Ibrahima Konate at the conclusion of his contract and the on-going injury issues at right-back.

Liverpool believe Araujo's experience – he was named Barcelona captain in January – is important and, significantly, he is up to speed having been involved in the Catalans' pre-season preparations and it is understood he will join squad training later this week.

He arrives having won three league titles with Barcelona, as well as two Copas del Rey, and wants to continue that at Anfield after the 2025 Premier League winners finished trophyless in a season which cost head coach Arne Slot his job just 12 months after lifting the title.

'Without a shadow of a doubt, the aim is to win trophies, win things. Liverpool is a team that is competing on all levels for all trophies, so we need to be battling it out on all fronts,' added Araujo, who has already received goodwill messages from two other Uruguayans who played for the club in Luis Suarez and Darwin Nunez.

'You aim high at a club like this – that's what we'll all be doing. As well as aiming high, I'll be giving everything that I can out there on the pitch to try to make that happen.'

Andoni Iraola has sought to address his defensive crisis with a number of centre halves injured

Araujo's arrival gives head coach Andoni Iraola greater depth in defence than his predecessor as new arrival Jeremy Jacquet is expected to return to training after a knee injury while Giovanni Leoni is entering the final stages of his rehabilitation following an ACL injury.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Ndiaye, both 18, have impressed in pre-season but with Joe Gomez not fit for the start of the new campaign, Iraola needed another senior defender as, for much of last season, Liverpool had to play Van Dijk and Konate virtually every game.

Liverpool are continuing to actively look for more signings, with attack in need of reinforcement, and Araujo's fee-free arrival will not impact those plans.

They have an interest in Paris St Germain's Bradley Barcola but will not pay over the odds, in keeping with their self-sustaining model of seeking value in the market.

Sports.title: Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg break down - with French club Marseille left furious at ex-Tottenham man's change of heart
Sports.content:
Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg break down - with French club Marseille left furious at ex-Tottenham man's change of heart

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Daily Mail Sport understands Marseille's owners have been left furious by this change of heart. The French club, keen to raise funds for their own summer spending, provisionally agreed to selling the Dane to the Toon.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, has also become a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Villa director of football Damian Vidagany told German outlet Bild: 'Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans. We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.'

Talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the Newcastle deal

They have also missed out on top targets including Spain winger Victor Munoz, who opted to join Liverpool

Villa lost 2-1 to Bayern in a pre-season friendly in Hong Kong over the weekend and Palhinha came on as a substitute.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, star forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, the manager who saved them from relegation before transforming them into a Champions League club and their 56-year major trophy drought, then stepped down on July 31.

They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

Howe has since been replaced by a Jaissle, who joins from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli. The 38-year-old's previous coaching experiences include a two-year spell at RB Salzburg preceded by a short-term stint at Austrian side Liefering.

They have recouped north of £250million following the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and have made five signings this summer - goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal and have also lost key players in Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon too

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace at the High Court following a controversial banner displayed at Selhurst Park last season.

The Nottingham Forest owner on Monday lodged a claim for defamation against his club’s Premier League rivals that dates back to the 1-1 draw between the clubs last August.

The banner depicting Marinakis holding a gun to the head of Forest player Morgan Gibbs-White and carried the words ‘Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.’ Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to such allegations.

Palace were charged by the Football Association last November and while the banner was not specified as the reason for the charge, there are strict rules regarding messaging containing defamatory, political and offensive slogans.

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago, due to UEFA’s rules regarding multi-club ownership. Forest benefited from that decision and were promoted into the Europa League.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is pursuing a defamation case against Crystal Palace

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago

The Gibbs-White/Marinakis banner appeared while that row was still fresh in the clubs’ minds.

Then Oliver Glasner, who led Palace to three trophies before departing at the end of last season, was promptly hired by Forest on a three-year deal. Palace host Forest in the Premier League on October 10.

‘This claim has been issued at Court shortly before the expiry of the one-year limitation period in defamation which could indicate that prior efforts to resolve the dispute have been unsuccessful,’ said Jamie Hurworth, a defamation specialist for law firm Payne Hicks Beach.

‘One of the first steps will be for the Court to determine how a reasonable reader would have interpreted the allegations on the banner which included an image of a gun being held to a player’s head, and whether that allegation is defamatory.

‘There will also be a potentially novel legal issue to address given the banner was held up by Crystal Palace fans, rather than perhaps any allegations being made by or on behalf of the club itself.’

Crystal Palace have declined to comment.

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt stormed to European Championships gold with a blistering effort in the 100m, finishing in 11 seconds flat - having been in fifth at the 50m mark.

It's the latest statement of intent in a burgeoning career that could see the Grantham-born sprinter reach the pinnacle of her sport.

Prior to her triumph on Monday night, Daily Mail Sport sat down with the 'sexy and aggressive' athlete on her remarkable rise.

Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Aston Villa dealt blow in loan pursuit of Real Madrid star Endrick - with Jose Mourinho making a decision on Brazilian forward's future
Sports.content:
Aston Villa dealt blow in loan pursuit of Real Madrid star Endrick - with Jose Mourinho making a decision on Brazilian forward's future

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa's hopes of taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid have been dashed by the LaLiga club's decision to keep him.

The Brazilian forward's future had been in limbo, with the youngster waiting to see if he is part of Jose Mourinho's plans for this season as he wants to establish himself in Madrid.

Had Mourinho not included Endrick in his plans, he may have been forced to seek a temporary move away as he did last season with Lyon.

But Daily Mail Sport understands that the legendary former Chelsea boss wants to include Endrick in his first team plans moving forwards, dealing a hammer blow to any pursuit from Villa.

The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024 after he turned 18, with a deal having been agreed two years before.

He has scored seven goals in 40 appearances for Los Blancos but joined Lyon for the second half of 2025-26 after struggling for regular gametime.

Endrick impressed in France, netting five goals and adding seven assists in 16 appearances.

Aston Villa are among the list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid

Real boss Jose Mourinho is set to make a decision on the Brazilian forward in the near future

That form was enough for him to earn a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, yet despite significant clamour back home, the 20-year-old only played 111 minutes at the tournament.

Endrick failed to score during that time as Carlo Ancelotti's side suffered an embarrassing exit in the last-16 stage at the hands of Norway.

Villa are looking for attacking reinforcements following the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans this summer, while there is uncertainty over the future of backup striker Tammy Abraham.

Ollie Watkins was also linked with Fenerbahce last month and Unai Emery's side sold Lucas Digne to PSG over the weekend.

They have so far added Switzerland World Cup breakout star Johan Manzambi and Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes.

Emery's side kick off their season with the UEFA Super Cup against PSG on Wednesday night, before they travel to Brighton next weekend in the Premier League.

‌



The new manager discussed the need to sign attacking stars in July, admitting that the Reds will need to be flexible in the transfer market. He said: "No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad. There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected

Jamie Vardy is a man without a club after leaving Cremonese and West Ham have him on their shortlist as they seek to add a new striker before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy could find himself back in England at the age of 39

West Ham are considering making a move for veteran frontman Jamie Vardy if they are unsuccessful with their pursuit of Troy Parrott.

‌



The former Leicester City forward wants to remain playing and is a free agent after his contract with Italian side Cremonese expired. It was his first spell playing outside of England and the Hammers could present the 39-year-old with the chance to return.

‌



Currently West Ham, who are gearing up for a first year in the Championship for more than a decade, have their sights on Parrott, formerly of Tottenham. The Irishman is now playing for AZ Alkmaar, where he has scored 51 goals in his two seasons.

‌



The Times reports that they've had a bid of £15million rejected and, if the Dutch side hold firm and refuse to sell their striker, then it could open the door for Vardy to make a move to the London Stadium. Another player on their shortlist was Wilson Isidor, but Sunderland have insisted he is not leaving.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Vardy spent the bulk of his career with the Foxes and was on their books when they won promotion from the Championship in 2014, he scored 16 times that year. Within two years he was a Premier League winner and proved himself to be a prolific marksman in the top flight.

Vardy scored 145 times in the top flight, putting him 14th on the all-time list, whilst he also won the Golden Boot in 2020. The former Fleetwood striker would win another Championship title with Leicester in 2022, scoring 20 times, and his experience could prove an asset for the Hammers as they seek an immediate return to the Premier League.

‌



The Hammers have just announced the signing of Manor Solomon, who penned a three-year deal after finalising a £7m switch from Tottenham. The winger was on loan at Leeds when they won promotion from the Championship in 2025.

View 2 Images West Ham are currently chasing Troy Parrott, but AZ Alkmaar have rejected their bids so far

West Ham are heavy favourites to win the Championship. They've managed to retain England international Jarrod Bowen whilst Nuno Espirito Santo has chosen to remain as manager. He won the second tier with Wolves back in 2017.

Sports.title: Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp

Rangers have endured a winless start to the season under new boss Derek McInnes but their chief executive has compared him to Jurgen Klopp in a shareholders meeting

View 2 Images Derek McInnes is yet to win as Rangers boss

Rangers shareholders were told to see Derek McInnes as "a Jurgen Klopp-type manager" by chief executive Jim Gillespie as he defended the under fire boss.

‌



McInnes was appointed at Ibrox off the back of a stellar spell at Hearts, that saw him come within minutes of winning the Scottish title last year, only to be upset by Celtic in a dramatic final day. They were still able to finish above Rangers, who quickly moved to hire him.

‌



However, Rangers have endured a poor start to the season and Sunday's defeat at home to Hibernian means they are already five points off the pace set by bitter rivals Celtic after only two games.

‌



The Scottish giants have held a meeting of their shareholders and Gillespie's comparison of McInnes and Klopp has raised eyebrows. The German has just taken charge of his national side but is regarded among the greatest managers of the modern era.

When asked by a shareholder to explain what attracted the club to the McInnes Gillespie replied: “You have two types of managers — a Klopp-type manager and a [Pep] Guardiola type. We think Derek is a Klopp type, someone who plays front-foot football and wants to win. Derek is the only manager who ticked all our boxes.”

McInnes didn't attend the meeting, and when pressed on that club chief Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago but McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team, who are in Europa League qualifying action on Thursday.

‌



The new Rangers boss has come out fighting following their slow start and maintains that the team are not as bad as the outside noise suggests.

View 2 Images Klopp won the Premier League with Liverpool and is regarded as one of their greatest managers (Image: LAURENCE GRIFFITHS/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"We're not as bad as some people will be saying at the minute," he told Sky Sports. "And I think it's important that we just batten down the hatches, stay strong, stay together. We try, as a club, to come out of this window strong and we will.

Article continues below

"At the minute, we're trying to manage the situation. Some players are not quite as fit but we need to get them playing to get them fit. We're not at the start we wanted but we still plan to get the finish and the outcome that we want and we'll work towards that."

Sports.title: What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture
Sports.content:
What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture

Marcus Rashford's future remains the topic of plenty of speculation as he returns to Manchester United after spending last season out on loan

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has rejoined his Manchester United team-mates after a spell out on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

A few months ago, the idea of Marcus Rashford returning to the fold at Manchester United looked far-fetched. Strange things can happen in football, though, and the England international's Old Trafford comeback is right up there

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and looked poised for a permanent move to Spotify Camp Nou. However, the Catalan club let their £26m option expire.

‌



For as long as Ruben Amorim was in the United dugout, a return for the forward looked impossible. However, the arrival of Michael Carrick - a former team-mate of Rashford - has altered the picture.

‌



England's run to the World Cup semi-finals meant a later return for the 28-year-old than for some of his colleagues. Now, though, Rashford's future is very much at the forefront of discussions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Man Utd return

Following United's 1-1 draw with PSG on Saturday, Carrick confirmed that Rashford has returned as part of his first team group, alongside Kobbie Mainoo.

‌



“We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together," United's manager said. “Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

View 3 Images Rashford has joined the United camp in Dublin (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Get Man United's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Manchester United have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, i nspired by the club's heritage and featuring a classic polo collar with iconic adidas details.

‌



As reported by the MEN, the England pair joined Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt, Karl Darlow, JJ Gabriel and Tynan Thompson on a private jet to Dublin. Some of those players could play a part in United's midweek friendly with Leeds, with Martinez also expected in Dublin.

Transfer stance

Rashford is not interested in moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia, thereby limiting his options. He would only join a European side who can offer him Champions League football. There are only so many clubs capable of meeting the forward's demands and one of them, Barcelona, are already out of the running barring a big U-turn.

The fee might not be a huge obstacle, with the MEN suggesting £25m - a little less than the provisional sum agreed with Barca - potentially enough to do it. However, those close to Rashford are said to have suggested United are no longer desperate to sell.

‌



Rashford will be with the rest of the squad for United's final two pre-season friendlies, against Leeds on Wednesday and AC Milan on Saturday, and is expected to be around for the Premier League opener away at Hull on August 22.

View 3 Images Barcelona allowed their £26m transfer option to expire (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer/Getty Images)

Telling gesture

While some fans are prepared to wait and see when it comes to Rashford's future, others have been looking for clues wherever they can find them. One such clue comes on the squad number front, where the forward is set to wear No. 14 next term.

Article continues below

United have already given Matheus Cunha the No. 10 previously worn by the England international and there are no indications it will revert back to its previous owner. Rashford wore No. 14 at Barcelona, though, and the choice can be read as an indication that the club and Carrick consider him part of their plans.

The No. 14 shirt was vacant for United last season. The number was not reused when Christian Eriksen left the club, while previous holders include Jesse Lingard and Javier Hernandez.

Sports.title: Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title
Sports.content:
Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title

Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month

View Image Oleksandr Khyzhniak is a rising star

Oleksandr Khyzhniak, who many believe can follow in mentor Oleksandr Usyk's footsteps, will fight for his first title later this month.

‌



Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month. He will now headline the second boxing event put on by Usyk's promotional company Usyk 17 Promotions on August 22.

‌



The event, to be held at !FESTrepublic in Lviv, will be dedicated to the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence and Usyk said: “Thirty-five years of independent development is actually not a very long time. Twelve of those years have been lived under conditions of war. But look at how much we have already managed to achieve despite everything.

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

"Look at the incredible athletes we have — not only boxers, but Olympic champions and Paralympians. Artists, musicians, scientists. We want to remember our greatest victories, honour those who fought and continue to fight for our freedom, and show the entire world that Ukraine has been, is and will remain a country of strong, talented and unbreakable people.”

Sergey Lapin, who is guiding Khyzhniak in his professional career, added:“A first title fight is both a natural and an important step in Oleksandr’s professional career. He is ready for a new level of competition and to prove his quality in championship fights. For Usyk 17 Promotions, it is especially important that this stage of his journey begins in Ukraine — at our second boxing event in Lviv. Our goal is to build a platform in Ukraine where the strongest boxers can develop, win titles and confidently progress to the international level.”

Article continues below

The fight night's co-main event will feature Pavlo Illiusha while the undercard will include nine Usyk 17 Promotions boxers in Maksym Rudyk, Maksym Zymenko, Dmytro Lovchynskyi, Elvin Aliiev, Bohdan Tolmachov, Mykola Laktionov, Jamal Kuliev, Aider Abduraimov and Matvii Razhba.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
